Transmute

trans-MYOOT · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To transmute is to change into a different form or substance.

Alchemists once dreamed of a method to transmute common lead into gold.

Worked Example

The therapist encouraged her to transmute her grief into something productive, like the community garden she eventually built.

Transmute describes a fundamental change from one form or substance into something else entirely, whether it's a literal material or an abstract feeling.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

transform: To transform is the broad, everyday word for changing something thoroughly -- a coat of paint transforms a room, though the room stays a room. To transmute is stranger and more total: one substance or nature actually becomes another, the way alchemists hoped lead would become gold.

convert: To convert is to change something from one form or use to another in a practical, orderly way -- dollars into euros, a garage into a spare room, a file into a new format. To transmute is magical and total by comparison: the very substance turns into something else entirely.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

preserve: keep something unchanged

maintain: keep something in its existing state

Where it sits · how little of the original remains — adjust → transmute → annihilate

adjust vs. transmute: To adjust something is a small tweak -- a strap tightened, a schedule shifted -- and the thing stays fundamentally itself, a far more modest change than to transmute it into something else entirely.

annihilate vs. transmute: To annihilate something is to destroy it completely, the opposite of transmuting it into something new.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — trans-

prefix — trans-: across, beyond (Latin)

root — mut

root — mut: to change (Latin (mutare))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: trans- ("across") + mut ("to change") + -e = to change across into a different form.

Use the root in a new word: mutation

Use the root in a new word: mutation: The same root gives us "mutation," a change in form, especially a genetic one -- a word you already met earlier in this course.

The same mut- root appears in Immutable, which you already met earlier in this course -- something immutable is fixed and unchanging, meaning it can never be transmuted at all.
